questions: Do you have involuntary twisting or turning movements of your neck that you cannot stop or control?
Do these movements cause you any pain or discomfort?
Did these symptoms begin suddenly, or have they developed gradually over weeks to months?
Have you taken any new medications (like antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs) in the past few weeks before these movements started?
Did these neck movements start when you were a child or teenager?
Do you have any family members with similar movements or any neurological condition?
Do you ever notice your hands shaking or any other unusual movements?
Have you ever been told you have any liver problems?
Has the abnormal movement ever affected any other body part besides your neck, like your arm, leg, or jaw?
Do the neck movements stop completely when you are sleeping?
Has anyone in your extended family (aunts, uncles, cousins) ever had similar involuntary movements, even if mild?
Have you ever tried any treatment for these movements, such as injections or medications?
Do the movements seem to get worse during times of stress or anxiety?
orders: Passive range of motion of the neck - test rotation, lateral bending, and extension/flexion
Palpation and inspection of the sternocleidomastoid muscles bilaterally for any tightness, fibrosis, or asymmetry
Cervical spine X-ray (AP, lateral, and open-mouth odontoid views)
Complete liver function tests (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, albumin)
Brain MRI with specific attention to basal ganglia (T1, T2, FLAIR, SWI) - looking for brain iron accumulation, structural abnormalities, or atrophy patterns
Beta-galactosidase enzyme activity assay (leukocytes or fibroblasts)
